newsitem.title: POLAND: Unions at Polish refinery call off Friday strike.
newsitem.headline: Unions at Polish refinery call off Friday strike.

text.p: Unions at Poland's Gdansk refinery have called off a one-hour warning strike planned for Friday, the head of the Solidarity trade union at the refinery said on Thursday.
Andrzej Cenacewicz told Reuters the unions would only hang out flags and collect donations for workers of the bankrupt Gdansk Shipyard, 3,800 of whom face lay-offs.
"A longer protest with a work stoppage would be pointless since the refinery is scheduled to stop work in April for maintenance anyway," Cenacewicz said.

During the one-hour warning strike the refinery's unions had also wanted to protest against delays in giving them 15 percent of the company's shares for free as envisaged by the new privatisation law to come into force on April 8.

But Jerzy Kaminski, the head if the state oil holding Nafta Polska SA, which holds 75 percent of the refinery's shares, wrote in a Thursday letter to the unions that they should not worry about receiving the stock.

"Nafta Polska is acting to stage a series of extraordinary shareholders' meetings in the capital group as soon as the new privatisation law is in place to adjust the statutes of the firms to the new law," Kaminski said.
"In this context we do not see any threat to the interest of the refinery's employees with respect to the shares to which they are entitled," he wrote.
Preliminary figures show the Gdansk refinery's 1996 net profit falling 35 percent from 1995's 125 million zlotys.
Sales grew 12 percent last year to 3.2 billion zlotys.
Analysts have said the falling profitability of Polish refineries has been caused by the government's maintaining of official limits on fuel prices until last month despite high world crude prices.
